newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes retreat with WTI, cargo sold.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes retreat with WTI, cargo sold.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes tracked lower values for West Texas Intermediate (WTI) midday Monday, while downward pressure on Alaska crude eased slightly after a cargo sold at a lower discount.
BP America sold a full cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude to a major West Coast producer at $2.20 under December WTI, traders said. The barrels are slated for December delivery, they said
The previous ANS spot cargo sold at $2.30 a barrel of October WTI.
December cash WTI prides fell 15 cents from Friday to $23.30/23.40 a barrel, dampenened by heavy selling on NYMEX and light trade during the U.S. Veterans Day Holiday.
Traders talked Outright ANS prices between $20.10/20.40.
Line 63 crude fell 20 cents a barrel, also under pressure from lower WTI prices.
Wilmington remained at $18.15/$18.25 a barrel, while Kern River crude stayed $16.65/$16.85 a barrel.
